items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: So I went and got Sharky to make the records with me.

ctx.x: Well that was a jazz band. We didn't play anything but jazz up at the roof you see. And I played drums and a conette just like I did later in California with Austin. But when it come to make the record well I didn't have nerve enough. I didn't think I played good enough you know. So I went and got Sharky to make the records with me. But he never did work in that band.

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: I was with Sharky at the time, at the Dream Room, and we were doubling with Buddy Rich.

ctx.x: But you didn't think solos belong then.

How do you feel about it now? I still don't like them. I still, I tell you, you have to do them. But I never did go. I'll take four bars, or maybe eight bars. But no, no, no chorus or choruses. Or anything like that. Because I still don't think it did. It's not a, it's not a, it's not a, an instrument for a solo. It's not a melodia. You can't get any melody out of it. Although I've heard some boys do some wonderful things. Pete Fountain had a boy here. I first heard him with Tex Banerke. And he's the only one who…

Monk, I want to get back, and we'll talk some more about, uh, drumming and, and jazz in, in general, but, uh, let's listen to, to one record, and I want to get your evaluation of it. stuff like stuff The End The End The End The End Okay, that was Charleston, of course. It's a band that Bob Thiel put together in New York to kind of spoof, I guess, old-time...

items.title: Sharkey Bonano Interview, 1966-11-09
items.q: Yes, I played with Monk on the Bienville Roof.

ctx.x: Did you play there with Monk on the Bienville Roof for a while?

Yes, I played with Monk on the Bienville Roof. We had, in fact we had two trumpets on the roof but we only had one trumpet when we made the record. Yeah. The other trumpet player, his name was Charlie Wagner.
Oh I've heard of him, he was out in Metry, he died just a year or two ago.
